newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges lower with pricing game seen.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges lower with pricing game seen.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges fetched lower prices on Tuesday but traders said the levels were connnected to price manoeuvering by market players.

High sulphur barges traded at $86 fob Rotterdam at least five times -- some $1.50 weaker than Monday's highest deal -- then were dealt further down at 50 cent intervals to exchange hands at $85.50, $85, $84.50 and $84 a tonne.
Traders said the high prices were done by a major while the low numbers by a trading house, which was also still reported to be having problems with physical deliveries.
"Someone is trying to set a lower number and another party interested in a high quotation bid the $86. That's the game in Rotterdam," one said. "It is not connected to physical cargoes".
A second trader said "the real market is $85/$86".
Traders put total demand at 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes.
No deals were reported early in high sulphur cargoes, which traders have said were softer with a shut arb to the United States and with prompt Russian material coming out.
Traders said some Russian barrels will be on the market soon, one E-4 loader out of St. Petersburg and three straight-run M-100 loading June 20 and 25.
These were exepcted to be offered at high numbers, around the $87 a tonne cif Rotterdam mark.
